H1_laugh_temporal_signature.claim: Measured laughs are preceded by longer-than-baseline pauses (DPV: laugh fires at the temporal violation).
H1_laugh_temporal_signature.data: 5 Kill Tony sets, word-level timing + laugh timestamps (characters2/theory/scribe/)
H1_laugh_temporal_signature.note: Every set independently shows the effect (5.2x to 54x). The laugh fires at the temporal violation, not after it.

H2_speech_rate_drop_into_pause.claim: Speech slows into the pause before a laugh, then accelerates after (fermata-then-rush).
H2_speech_rate_drop_into_pause.data: 8 laughs with clean pre-pause / post-laugh windows (KT sets)
H2_speech_rate_drop_into_pause.note: n=8 too small for significance but direction is consistent: slow into the hold, fast out of it.

H3_punch_two_part_signature.claim: Norrick (punch faster) and DPV (extended pause) are sequential, not competing: HOLD, then SNAP.
H3_punch_two_part_signature.data: Louis Road Rage (12 punches) + Norm Moth (4 punches), measured word-timing
H3_punch_two_part_signature.verdict: SUPPORTED — both mechanisms fire, in sequence
H3_punch_two_part_signature.note: The pause before the punch is 1.4-2x the set's mean pause (DPV). The punch itself is delivered 1.48x faster than the speech before it (Norrick). The temporal signature of a punch is: extended hold, then acceleration. Fermata, then rush.

H4_content_coupling_paper_scores.claim: benign_violation (BV sweet spot) correlates with incongruity x surprise coupling.
H4_content_coupling_paper_scores.note: Paper-scored BV is too sparse (9% nonzero) and misaligned to test coupling. Surprise alone predicts punch_pos strongly (r=0.46). The coupling hypothesis is better tested (and IS supported) via H1/H3 on measured timing. Honest negative on the paper labels; the theory survives via the measured-data path.

H5_punch_syllable_compression.claim: Punches have fewer syllables per word than setups (Seinfeld's syllable-shaving).
H5_punch_syllable_compression.note: No syllable-density difference within bits. Seinfeld's claim is about inter-joke TRANSITIONS fitting a time budget, not intra-bit punch compression. Reframe needed: the right test is whether punch WORD COUNT fits a consistent time slot, not syllable density.

confirmed: Laughs fire at temporal violations (14x baseline pause, p<0.0001)
Punches have a two-part signature: extended hold (1.4-2x baseline) then acceleration (1.48x, p=0.045)
directional: Speech slows into the pause, accelerates out (n=8, p=0.069)
not_supported: Intra-bit punch syllable compression (wrong test for Seinfeld's claim)
summary.thesis_impact: H1+H3 confirm the core claim: timing is structural, not decorative. The punch's temporal signature (hold + snap) is measurable and consistent across two very different comedians (Louis slow-confessional, Norm never-stop). The geometric metric needs both pause-before and rate-at-punch as components.
